items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: They claimed that it was fantastic, said they had the best music and the best everything, dancers, comedians, but they had everybody: Flip Wilson, John Kirby, they’d have all — I guess I don’t know about Richard Pryor, but they had all the best of everything, the best dancers and everything.

ctx.x: Yeah. I remember seeing a documentary about Vegas and I think you’re correct, somehow that happened.

Uh huh. They claimed that it was fantastic, said they had the best music and the best everything, dancers, comedians, but they had everybody: Flip Wilson, John Kirby, they’d have all — I guess I don’t know about Richard Pryor, but they had all the best of everything, the best dancers and everything.

That’s very interesting. I wanted to ask you something you briefly touched on before. You were talking about rock & roll. You know musical styles and what’s popular changes a lot but do you remember specifically what it felt like for jazz-based musicians around here when rock & roll started to take over?
